subject: economics
title: Spot the Difference Adventure
welcome_lead: What do you need? What do you just want? ✅
meta_desc: Needs vs Wants Adventure 1 — KS3 Economics on the basic difference between needs and wants.
final_note: You learned to spot needs vs wants and why it matters for spending.

concepts.def: Nice to have but not vital

walkthroughs.body_html:
A need is something you must have to live or function:

  • Food and water.
  • Clothes.
  • Shelter.
  • School.

These are essentials. 🥪

A want is something nice to have:

  • Designer trainers.
  • Latest console.
  • Cinema trip.
  • Holiday.

These are luxuries. 🎮

Smart spending puts priority on needs first.

Pay for the school trip lunch before the new game.

Once needs are sorted, wants are fun.

mcqs.q: What does dependency theory argue about development?
options: Demand always falls when supply increases.

Poorer 'periphery' countries are kept underdeveloped by their economic relationships with rich 'core' countries — through unequal trade, debt and historical colonialism. It challenges the view that integration with rich economies automatically helps.
Dependency theory is about households relying on benefits.
Dependency theory means poor countries are simply lazy.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between fixed and variable costs?
options: Fixed costs don't change with output (e.g. rent, salaries); variable costs change directly with output (e.g. raw materials, hourly wages).
Fixed costs never change at all, ever.
Dependency theory is about households relying on benefits.
Fixed costs are paid once and variable costs are paid daily.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a shift in demand and a movement along the demand curve?
options: A change in price shifts the demand curve.
A movement along the curve is caused by a change in price; a shift of the whole curve is caused by changes in other factors (income, tastes, substitute prices).
Fixed costs are paid once and variable costs are paid daily.
Demand always falls when supply increases.
